# National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) – Summary
The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), founded in 1910, is the largest and one of the most prestigious universities in Latin America. Established as a secular, national institution, it merged Mexico City’s decentralized colleges to reorganize higher education and has played a pivotal role in Mexico’s social, political, and cultural development. With its main campus, Ciudad Universitaria, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, UNAM boasts many satellite campuses and international extension schools. The university is home to multiple museums (such as the Palacio de Minería, San Ildefonso Museum, and National Biodiversity Pavilion), cultural centers, and research observatories.
UNAM offers a wide array of undergraduate, graduate, and high school programs, with over 324,000 students enrolled. It is renowned for its numerous schools and colleges, including fields in sciences, engineering, medicine, law, architecture, arts, and social sciences. UNAM hosts robust research institutes and centers covering disciplines like astronomy, biotechnology, nuclear sciences, and renewable energies, contributing over half of Mexico’s scientific output and maintaining international research competitiveness. The university is recognized globally, consistently ranking as the top university in Mexico and among the highest in Latin America.
UNAM has produced notable alumni, including presidents of Mexico, Nobel laureates such as Octavio Paz, Alfonso García Robles, and Mario Molina, and world leaders in science, arts, and politics. It fosters a vibrant student life with cultural traditions (such as the Day of the Dead offerings), numerous student associations and sports teams (notably the successful Pumas football and volleyball teams). Its seal, motto "For my people the spirit shall speak," and puma emblem symbolize its commitment to cultural identity, education, and research. UNAM has a history of political activism and inclusivity, and is widely known for its advocacy for minority empowerment and women in STEM.
